the question of what kind of new particles can be dark matter if the scattering off nucleons in current and future direct detection experiments is spin-dependent.

the LHC is the most powerful probe for dark matter candidates with primarily spin-dependent interactions.

if the dark matter particle interacts with nucleons primarily through spin-dependent interactions, then it is likely that there are new particles with Standard Model quantum number close to the weak mass scale, or a $Z'$ boson with mass close to the TeV scale.
